- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was high recently — if so, apply downward bias correction.
- If true outcome is significantly above forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was low — if so, apply upward bias correction.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days) — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for first 3 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings, model often misreads momentum — apply mean reversion bias: forecast = (last 5 days avg + 0.5×current sentiment) if sentiment is volatile.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above true outcome, reduce by 2–3% for next 7-day window if sentiment is neutral or negative.
